HSTU (2024) provides a natural temporal backbone: SiLU-based attention with learned relative position/time biases and multiplicative feature gating. Its temporal bias can represent elapsed-time effects without imposing universal recency decay. The implementation’s time-aware setup requires consistent query-time availability during training and inference; held-out next-purchase timestamps must not become inputs unless the benchmark supplies them. [HSTU paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152), [RecTools implementation documentation](https://rectools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/examples/tutorials/transformers_HSTU_tutorial.html).

Recent work supports separating temporal scales. Decoupled Temporal Encoding (2026) distinguishes broad temporal dynamics from local sequence order, activating relative-order bias when interactions are temporally dense. TSRec (2025) models repeat consumption through both interval relationships and sequential patterns. These motivate testing jointly trained, content-conditioned time gates inside one HSTU network, allowing persistent history influence alongside short-lived local dependencies. This is an architectural hypothesis, not evidence that learned gates identify psychological intent. [DTE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16274), [TSRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08531).

Replenishment and complementary purchases also argue against treating every purchase as a satisfied need. Repurchase research reports multiple periodicities, while complementary/substitution modeling studies relationships beyond recent interests. Neither establishes such mechanisms in these four Amazon categories. Use only observed histories, timestamps and available text; evaluate temporal gates through fixed validation HR@10 and controlled ablations. History-removal sensitivity measures predictive dependence, not causal intent; direct replenishment benefits may be limited when recommendations exclude previously seen items. [Repurchase-cycle study](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1567422326000037), [Complementary/substitution study](https://xbzrb.hbu.edu.cn/EN/10.3969/j.issn.1000-1565.2024.05.012).
